Theme

Church life

soul noun

also souls, the soul

classical

Sall. J. 2.2: ingeniī facinora, sīcut anima, immortālia sunt (Lewis & Short)
Vulg. Lc. 1.46

anima, animae f.

noun, first declension

the soul

The breath of life, and the soul that outlives the body (Sall.); the Church’s word for the soul (Magnificat anima mea Dominum). The plural’s dative and ablative are animīs, in the Church also animābus (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • animus, animī m. — the mind, the spirit

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

    The thinking and feeling soul, the mind; anima is the soul as life itself (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Magnificat anima mea Dominum

    My soul magnifies the LordVulg. Lc. 1.46

  • Benedīc, anima mea, Dominō

    Bless the Lord, my soulVulg. Ps. 102 (103), 2

  • angusta est domus animae meae quō veniās ad eam: dīlātētur abs tē. ruīnōsa est: refice eam

    the house of my soul is too small for you to come into: let it be enlarged by you. It is falling down: rebuild itAug. Conf. 1.5.6

See also heaven, God, sin.
